correctness.rationale: On arbitrary P2 initial laws, E(mu)=1/2 sum_i(a_i m_i²+b_i v_i), b_i=a_i+beta_i/2, and selected-coordinate affine pushforward multiplies mean and centered modes by 1-eta_i a_i and 1-eta_i b_i. Their squared worst-case modal multiplier is uniquely minimized by eta_i=2/(a_i+b_i). At that step both squared multipliers equal t_i=((b_i-a_i)/(b_i+a_i))² in (0,1), so for visit counts N_i(k), E_k=sum_i E_i(0)t_i^{N_i(k)}. IID visits give E[E_k]=sum_i E_i(0)(1-p_i(1-t_i))^k, hence the worst-case k-step factor is max_i(1-p_i delta_i)^k; the simultaneous SLLN gives the almost-sure worst-case factor max_i(t_i^{p_i}). Equalizing p_i delta_i and p_i(-log t_i) separately yields the unique inverse-delta annealed and inverse-log quenched policies, respectively, for every k and every d>=2. The source proves the attained annealed expectation is (1-1/sum_j delta_j^-1)^k E0 for ALL initial laws and quenched rate exp(-1/sum_j c_j^-1). This is a modal proof for all dimensions, not an inference from finite tests. Independently checked the d=2 rational instance beta1=1/1000,beta2=4: t=(1/16008001,1/4), annealed p1=16008001/37352001, RA=7114667/12450667, tending to p1=3/7 and RA=4/7 as beta1 downarrow0, while quenched p1 ->0 and its expected worst-case factor ->1.

originality.rationale: The precise two-minimax separation for nonprojective affine Wasserstein coordinate maps is not entailed by Xu--Li general convergence bounds, by expected-rate optimized Euclidean SPD coordinate descent, or by Kaczmarz abstracts merely distinguishing expectation from typical rates. The model is a diagonal special case of Xu--Li, but the scientific contribution is the exact simultaneous two-risk optimization and incompatible sampling policies. Full text of a historically plausible Kaczmarz source was not obtained, leaving documented priority risk.
residual_risks: The historical Agaskar--Wang--Lu 2014 randomized Kaczmarz complete article remains insufficiently inspected; an abstract cannot exclude a transferable reciprocal-log result.
Outside diagonal strictly positive exact-gradient fixed-iid coordinate probabilities, the formulas do not apply; the nearly-zero interaction parameter limit is not attained inside beta1>0.

value.rationale: Expected-error guarantees and almost-sure sample-path error decay are genuinely distinct performance objectives; the sharp minimax sampling rules and the limiting 4/7-vs-1 separation explain precisely why choosing one can be adverse to the other, for all initial probability laws in the stated natural diagonal Wasserstein model. This is a quantitative algorithm-design tradeoff, not a renamed convergence bound.
